ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Cars A and B at a certain moment start linear motion from the same place along the same direction. Taking this moment as the timing starting point, according to the x-t graph in the figure, what is the positional relationship of the two cars at time $t_1$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: At time $t_1$, car B catches up with car A from behind

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Cars A and B at a certain moment start linear motion from the same place along the same direction. Taking this moment as the timing starting point, according to the x-t graph in the figure, what is the positional relationship of the two cars at time $t_1$?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: At time $t_1$, car B catches up with car A from behind
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an x-t graph, the vertical axis is position x, and the horizontal axis is time t. The graph lines of cars A and B both start from the origin O, indicating that they start from the same place at the same moment; A's graph line is an oblique straight line, and B's graph line is an upward-curving curve. At the vertical dashed line corresponding to t1 in the figure, the two graph lines of A and B intersect; before t1, B's curve is below A's straight line. Reasoning: In an x-t graph, the ordinate of a graph line at the same moment represents the position at that moment. At time t1 the two graph lines intersect, indicating that the position coordinates of cars A and B are the same; and before t1 B's graph line is below A's, indicating that B's position coordinate is smaller than A's, that is, B is behind car A. As time reaches t1, car B reaches the same position as car A, so car B catches up with car A from behind.
